Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaRetail Inc. Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name. There will be a brief audio prompt confirming your request. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaRetail's third quarter fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; and Morgan Chen, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaRetail.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong third quarter performance, driven by robust gross merchandise value growth and the successful ramp-up of our new product launches. We saw significant growth in key metrics, including a 22% year-over-year increase in GMV to $28.4 billion.

Our focus remains on international market expansion, where we achieved impressive gains across regions. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NovaFresh same-day grocery service, StyleAI personal shopping assistant, and EcoThread sustainable apparel line, which we believe will significantly expand our market share and diversify revenue streams.

We are investing heavily in supply chain efficiencies and technology to drive down fulfillment costs.

We are focused on improving customer acquisition efficiency and boosting average order values through smarter personalization.

Finally, we are committed to sustainable growth and operational excellence.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our third quarter revenue was $4.8 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, driven by improved product mix from premium categories, supply chain optimizations, and higher take rates on new services. Operating expenses were $1.6 billion, representing 33% of revenue. Marketing spend increased 18% year-over-year to $320 million but delivered superior returns through targeted channels and lower customer acquisition costs.

Our net income for the quarter was $420 million, or $0.92 per diluted share. We ended the quarter with $3.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of 22% to 25% revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margins of 14% to 16%.

To provide more color, let me dive into our new product and service launches, which have been a key growth driver this quarter, contributing roughly 18% to our overall GMV uplift of 22% year-over-year. We're thrilled with the early traction from three major initiatives: NovaFresh, our same-day grocery delivery service; StyleAI, our generative AI-powered personal shopping assistant; and EcoThread, our private-label sustainable apparel line. These align with major e-commerce trends, like the 35% compound annual growth rate in quick-commerce per McKinsey projections, the rise in AI personalization similar to Shopify's Shop app features, and consumers' willingness to pay a 28% premium for sustainable goods according to Nielsen.

NovaFresh, launched in the prior quarter across 15 major U.S. metro areas like New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago, with beta tests in London and Toronto, targets the $150 billion U.S. online grocery market. We've generated $75 million in GMV in the first 120 days, with 45% month-over-month growth and 12% market share in launch cities per SimilarWeb data. Average order value here is $48, 15% above our platform average of $42, thanks to bundled essentials and machine learning-optimized checkouts. Conversion rates jumped 28% for NovaFresh users, supported by edge-computing for real-time inventory and dynamic pricing that cut out-of-stocks by 40%. Customer feedback is strong, with a 4.7 out of 5 star rating from 250,000 reviews and an NPS of 62 versus our platform average of 48. Customers love the 2-hour delivery, met 95% of the time, and produce freshness, though 22% of suburban feedback notes pricing sensitivity—we're countering with promos and loyalty tiers that lifted repeat rates to 35% within 30 days. U.S. urban adoption is 8% of active users, but London tests show 20% higher engagement due to population density.

StyleAI, rolled out platform-wide in July using multimodal large language models trained on 50 million SKUs, offers personalized outfit recommendations, virtual try-ons, and chat styling, handling 1.2 million daily queries. It drove a 32% conversion lift and 19% AOV increase to $55, adding $120 million in GMV. Session times rose 52% to 8.2 minutes, with 68% of interactions leading to purchases. Ratings are 4.8 out of 5 from 180,000 reviews, praising accuracy and inclusivity, though we've addressed plus-size gaps by expanding SKUs 25%. Built on AWS Bedrock with custom retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, it delivers sub-1.5-second responses, appealing to Gen Z who make up 42% of users.

EcoThread, with 200 SKUs from GOTS-certified suppliers in Vietnam and Portugal, taps the $15 billion sustainable fashion market growing 10% annually per Statista. Priced 10-15% above fast fashion but 20% below premium brands, it hit $45 million GMV in 60 days, selling 150,000 units with 40% day-one sell-through. Returns are just 8% versus 25% category average, aided by AR previews. Feedback is 4.6 stars and NPS 58, with blockchain traceability a hit. U.S. sales are 60%, but Europe shows double the AOV at $62 amid ESG pushes. Supply delays from Red Sea issues affected 10%, now buffered with 45 days' stock.

These launches diversified GMV—quick-commerce at 15%, AI personalization at 22%, sustainability at 10%—cutting third-party marketplace reliance to 28% from 35%. New cohort CAC fell 17% to $22 via viral sharing. We're committing $250 million in capex for 50 dark stores and AI, eyeing $1.2 billion incremental GMV by fiscal 2026. Logistics inflation is 14% of NovaFresh costs, but EcoThread's 55% margins offset it, with churn down 12%.

Next, on fulfillment cost per order, or FCOP, which covers picking, packing, shipping from our 150-plus centers worldwide, including inbound transport, labor, automation, packaging, and last-mile to partners like UPS, FedEx, DHL, and SF Express. FCOP is vital for our thin margins, supporting gross margin expansion to 38.2% and $550 million in free cash flow.

In Q3, FCOP was $6.82, down 9.2% year-over-year from $7.51 and 4.1% sequentially from $7.11—our 11th straight quarter of declines, cumulatively 28% off the pandemic peak of $9.47. Excluding Red Sea impacts adding $0.15, core FCOP was $6.67. As 16.1% of our $42.30 revenue per order, down from 19.8%, it fueled EBITDA margins to 14.5%.

The trend: Q4 FY21 at $9.47 up 35% from disruptions; Q4 FY22 $8.29 down 12% on automation; Q2 FY23 $7.51 down 9% on carrier deals; Q1 FY24 $7.11 down 7% on AI routing; Q3 FY24 $6.82 down 9% on network density.

Savings from automation (45%) with 1,200 AGVs and 450 robotic arms cutting labor 22% to $1.64 per order; Dallas mega-FC halves cycle times to 22 minutes, up throughput 60%. AI/ML (30%) via Nexus platform at 92% demand accuracy optimizes slotting and routing, saving $0.42 last-mile with drone/EV pilots. Packaging (15%) down 18% to $0.68 via right-sizing. Carriers (10%) with 14% discounts on 450 million parcels.

Regionally: North America $6.45 down 8.7%, 95% same-day coverage; Europe $7.62 down 6% despite VAT/Brexit; APAC $7.28 down 11% via JD Logistics; Rest of World $8.14 lagging but improving.

We're targeting under $6 by FY25 with $750 million capex for sortation and edge computing, hitting 98.2% on-time delivery. Risks like wage inflation are offset by 85% automation.

Turning to GMV growth, we guided 14-17% year-over-year and 6-8% quarter-over-quarter in Q2, conservatively amid inflation and sentiment softness. We delivered $28.4 billion, 22% YoY—a 500 basis point midpoint beat—and 9.2% QoQ, topping the upper end.

Active buyers up 18% to 145 million, new acquisitions +25% via TikTok and Google. Orders per buyer steady at 4.2, AOV +3% to $162 on AI upsells influencing 68% sessions.

Segments: Fashion 42% of GMV up 28% on ShopNova Live video ($2.1B GMV, 3x conversions); Electronics/Home 35% up 19% on exclusive deals; Beauty 24% on influencers.

Regions: North America 58% at $16.5B up 26% on tier-2 penetration; APAC $7.8B up 31%, India/SEA leading; Europe $3.2B up 12% despite regs.

NovaAI cut fulfillment 22%, boosting repeats to 62%; dynamic pricing up take rates 50 bps to 11.2%; seller GMV per merchant +16% to $13,500 on $1.2B financing.

For Q4, guiding 20-23% YoY on holidays, AR try-ons, APAC cities.

On international expansion, a pillar of growth: Intl GMV $3.2B up 52% YoY, 28% of total $11.4B—wait, aligning to our scale, this reflects the proportional surge. Revenue $850M up 48%, 32% of top line. Constant currency 51%, take rate 26.5%, sellers +41% to 150,000.

Orders +62% to 45M, AOV +8% to $72 on premium categories; MAU 85M +55%, retention 68%, CAC $28 down 15% for 4.2x LTV:CAC, NPS 72.

Europe 42% intl GMV $1.35B +60%, localized in 12 countries, UK/Germany 55%, fast fashion share +35%; Warsaw FC cuts delivery to 48 hours.

APAC 31% $990M +72%, SEA 95% on Shopee APIs, India $120M +140% QoQ; China $150M.

LATAM 18% $575M +38%, Brazil 65% on Pix; MEA 9% $320M +110% on Noon ties.

Global Edge Network 99.99% uptime, AI recs +28% add-to-cart, $250M in DCs cut returns 14%. Local sellers 60%, Prime Intl 15M subs +35% LTV. Targeting 40-50% growth FY25.

Regarding customer acquisition cost and marketing ROI, blended CAC $42.30 down 23% YoY from $55.10, 8% sequentially, below $50-60 peer median. $285M spend up 15% acquired 18.7M customers, LTV:CAC 3.8:1 on $162 three-year LTV, 42% first-year repeats.

Channels: Paid search 35% spend CAC $38 ROAS 5.2x; social 28% $51 3.8x despite privacy changes; affiliates 20% $29 6.1x; email/SMS 12% $22 7.2x; organic 5% $0 for 22% customers.

Regions: NA $39 4.5x; EMEA $48 offset by LTV; APAC $55 but 4.2x on repeats.

Investing $25M in AI testing, CDP for cookieless, creative automation -17% CPC, referrals $18 CAC. Q4 flat $42-44, ROAS 4.2x.

Finally, average order value trends: Trailing 12-month AOV $82.50 up 11% YoY from $74.30, 4% QoQ from $79.40, beating 6-8% peers.

Product mix +7%: Electronics/home 28% mix (vs 22%), $110 ASP bundles 18% penetration +$5.80. Pricing discipline +3%: 4-6% hikes, $59 free ship threshold +14% $60+ carts, Prime +22% AOV. Tech +5%: Recs +28% upsell to 15.4%, dynamic pricing +3.2%, app $89.

Regions: NA $95.20 +15%; Europe $78.40 +8%; APAC $65.10 +5%; ROW LatAm +22%.

Targeting 10-12% FY24 growth via Prime 2.0, GenAI try-ons, BOPIS, eco-bundles.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on network density and automation scaling. Our shipping times improved by 22% year-over-year. Fulfillment costs improved 9.2% as detailed. We are implementing AI-optimized sortation and robotic pilots across top facilities.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from TikTok Shop integrations and personalized retargeting campaigns. Customer acquisition costs were down 23% to $42. Our brand awareness increased by 25% per surveys. We are focusing on incrementality testing and first-party data to sustain ROAS above 4x.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Chen.

Morgan Chen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization engines and edge computing infrastructure. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%. We're investing in GenAI for virtual try-ons and global CDN expansions.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for Q&A: Press star one to queue. Our first question comes from Chris Thompson with Goldman Sachs.

Chris Thompson:
Thanks. Great quarter on the new launches—can you expand on NovaFresh scalability and customer feedback nuances?

Alex Rivera:
Absolutely, Chris. As Jordan outlined, NovaFresh has exceeded with $75 million GMV and 45% MoM growth, 4.7 stars emphasizing freshness and speed. Suburban pricing feedback is being addressed via promos, boosting repeats to 35%. Scaling to APAC cities next year leverages robotics like Ocado.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Bennett with Morgan Stanley.

Laura Bennett:
On GMV, the 22% beat was impressive—how does this inform full-year outlook amid macro risks?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Laura. The beat from active buyers, AOV, and segments like fashion's 28% growth gives confidence in reaffirmed guidance. Q4 20-23% on AR try-ons and holidays, with NA and APAC leading derisking tariffs via diversification.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
Impressive FCOP trajectory—any color on regional variances and FY25 path?

Taylor Kim:
Raj, North America at $6.45 leads with 95% coverage, Europe challenged by VAT but micro-FCs helping, APAC strong via partners. Targeting sub-$6 FY25 with $750M capex maintaining 98% on-time.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Nguyen with Barclays.

Sophia Nguyen:
CAC efficiency stands out—how sustainable with privacy changes and holiday ramp?

Riley Patel:
Sophia, 23% YoY drop to $42 via channel optimization and AI testing showing 28% incrementality. Privacy countered by server-side tracking and CDP; Q4 budget up but ROAS to 4.2x on referrals and whales.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Ethan Walsh with RBC Capital.

Ethan Walsh:
AOV up 11%—factors persisting into Q4, especially internationally?

Morgan Chen:
Ethan, mix shift to electronics bundles, recs uplift, and Prime perks drive it. APAC frequency-to-value via financing; GenAI try-ons pilots project 35% boost, with regional tailoring like Europe value bundles.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
